candidates.claim: Tensor Scrambling only applies when a dense operator is available and enough random samples can reveal always-zero elements; it is not suitable for stochastic or data-dependent black-box operators.
candidates.mechanism: Paper says Tensor Scrambling handles black-box operators by random scrambling and assumes a dense operator -> if the operator has random or data-dependent zeros, always-zero elements may not correspond to pruned elements -> propagation can infer incorrect sparsity.
candidates.conditions: Dense version of the operator is available; operator is deterministic enough; enough random samples are run.
candidates.consequence: Sparsity propagation may be expensive or inaccurate for black-box, stochastic, or stateful operators.
candidates.defeaters: If the operator is deterministic and a dense implementation exists with sufficient samples, the limitation is irrelevant.

candidates.claim: SparTA's compilation overhead is high for large models, especially transformation and specialization, which limits rapid design-space exploration.
candidates.mechanism: Paper reports BERT takes 3 minutes propagation, 2 hours transformation, and 1.5 hours specialization single-threaded -> iterative sparsity exploration requires repeated compilation -> high overhead slows exploration and may be impractical for larger models.
candidates.conditions: Large model; single-threaded compilation; repeated exploration.
candidates.consequence: Long compile times; reduced practicality for rapid iteration.
candidates.defeaters: Parallelization, pre-tuned kernels, or prior knowledge could reduce overhead.

quotes.quote: Taking BERT as an example, the propagation, transformation, and specialization take 3 minutes, 2 hours and 1.5 hours respectively using a single thread.
It is possible to reduce the overhead by leveraging more prior knowledge in transformation policy and pre-tuned kernels. We leave it as future work.

evidence.support_description: Taking BERT as an example, the propagation, transformation, and specialization take 3 minutes, 2 hours and 1.5 hours respectively using a single thread.
It is possible to reduce the overhead by leveraging more prior knowledge in transformation policy and pre-tuned kernels. We leave it as future work.

candidates.claim: WeightedBlockCover uses a greedy heuristic and profiled block weights; for very sparse operators the weights can be inaccurate, and fallback enumeration can blow up combinatorially.
candidates.mechanism: Paper uses greedy lowest-cost block cover and profiles block weights -> when operator is too sparse to saturate cores, weights are less accurate -> greedy choice may be suboptimal; enumerating all combinations can be expensive.
candidates.conditions: Multiple block sizes; profiling-based weights; very sparse operator.
candidates.consequence: Suboptimal block-size selection or high search cost.
candidates.defeaters: If operator is dense enough or block-size options are few, the limitation is minor.

quotes.quote: We use a simple greedy algorithm to pick the blocks with the lowest cost

When an operator is too sparse to saturate available cores, the weights may become less accurate. In such cases, we enumerate all the combinations of block sizes to run the weighted block cover algorithm and pick the best one.

candidates.claim: Attribute propagation's termination and correctness rely on monotonic, commutative, and associative propagation rules; non-monotonic or context-dependent sparsity rules are outside this guarantee.
candidates.mechanism: Paper guarantees termination because each propagation monotonically increases sparsity and rules are commutative/associative -> if a new rule is non-monotonic or order-dependent, the fixed-point algorithm may not terminate or may produce order-dependent results -> extensibility is constrained.
candidates.conditions: Propagation rules are monotonic, commutative, and associative.
candidates.consequence: New sparsity semantics that violate these properties may not be safely supported.
candidates.defeaters: If all registered rules satisfy the properties, the limitation does not apply.

quotes.quote: As each propagation monotonically increases sparsity and both the propagations of pruning and quantization are commutative and associative, Algorithm 1 is guaranteed to terminate.

evidence.support_description: As each propagation monotonically increases sparsity and both the propagations of pruning and quantization are commutative and associative, Algorithm 1 is guaranteed to terminate.

candidates.claim: Tensor Scrambling's probabilistic zero detection can misclassify elements when random sampling is insufficient or when zeros arise from operator semantics rather than pruning.
candidates.mechanism: Paper treats elements that always stay zero across random scrambles as pruned -> if sampling is too small, a truly nonzero element may never be observed nonzero; if operator produces structural zeros, they may be misread as pruning -> propagation can be wrong.
candidates.conditions: Enough random samples; zeros correspond to pruning; operator semantics do not create incidental zeros.
candidates.consequence: False pruning or missed pruning, leading to incorrect optimization or accuracy loss.
candidates.defeaters: If enough samples are used and operator zeros are semantically pruned, the risk is low.

candidates.claim: The evaluation covers only three models, four sparsity patterns, and three accelerators, so generalization to other model families, operators, and hardware is not established.
candidates.mechanism: Paper evaluates BERT, MobileNet, and HuBERT on CUDA GPU, ROCm GPU, and Intel CPU -> these do not cover all DNN workloads or accelerators -> performance and applicability may differ on untested models and hardware.
candidates.conditions: Target workload resembles evaluated models and hardware.
candidates.consequence: Speedup and memory claims may not transfer to other settings.
candidates.defeaters: Broader evaluation on the target workload would remove this limitation.

candidates.claim: SparTA does not guarantee accuracy; high sparsity can cause substantial accuracy drops, as shown for MobileNet unstructured sparsity.
candidates.mechanism: Paper reports MobileNet unstructured 95% sparsity drops accuracy from 78.27 to 64.15 -> SparTA optimizes latency and memory for a given sparse model -> if the sparsity algorithm's accuracy loss is unacceptable, speedups are not usable.
candidates.consequence: Speedups may come at unacceptable accuracy cost.
candidates.defeaters: If the application tolerates the accuracy drop or a better sparsity algorithm is used, the limitation is less relevant.

quotes.quote: For MobileNet, unstructured sparsity has a higher accuracy drop, as its sparsity is high (i.e., 95%).

evidence.support_description: For MobileNet, unstructured sparsity has a higher accuracy drop, as its sparsity is high (i.e., 95%).

candidates.claim: The quantization propagation's acceptable accuracy drop is attributed to knowledge distillation and information bottleneck, but the paper does not fully explain why specific layers can be reduced without loss.
candidates.mechanism: Paper uses calibration-based fine-tuning and cites information bottleneck -> it observes 18/28 layers reduce bit width with small accuracy drop -> the causal mechanism for which layers tolerate reduction is not fully characterized -> may not generalize.
candidates.conditions: Calibration data and fine-tuning; model similar to MobileNet.
candidates.consequence: Quantization propagation may be less predictable on other models.
candidates.defeaters: A validated theory or broader experiments could explain and remove the uncertainty.

candidates.claim: Leveraging Sparse Tensor Cores requires a strict 1x2 sparsity pattern and decomposes the tensor into two sub-Matmuls, so benefit is limited when the pattern does not match.
candidates.mechanism: Paper says Sparse Tensor Core requires one pruned element in a [1×2] tile -> generic unstructured sparsity must be split into a matching part and a remainder -> the remainder may be dense or low-sparsity, reducing gain and adding overhead.
candidates.conditions: Hardware Sparse Tensor Core; sparsity pattern can be decomposed; remainder kernel efficient.
candidates.consequence: Limited speedup or extra overhead for patterns not aligned with hardware.
candidates.defeaters: If the sparsity pattern already matches the hardware requirement, the limitation is irrelevant.

candidates.consequence: Limited applicability to non-einsum, control-flow, or stateful operators.
candidates.defeaters: If the target model uses only einsum-like operators, the limitation is irrelevant.

candidates.consequence: Compilation may be memory-intensive or slow.
